definition: The strategy used to set the initial values of a neural network's parameters before training begins.
details: Good initialization (e.g., Xavier/Glorot or He initialization) helps gradients flow properly at the start of training and can significantly affect convergence speed and final performance.

explainer.lead: Weight initialization is the strategy for setting a neural network's initial parameter values before training. It matters because good initialization helps gradients flow properly and affects convergence speed and final performance.

tiers.eli5: It is like placing the first stones of a path carefully so the rest of the path can be laid without hitting a wall.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick schemes such as Xavier/Glorot or He initialization matched to the layer's activation and fan-in. The pitfall is leaving defaults that suit a different activation, which can cause vanishing or exploding gradients early in training.
tiers.paperLevel: Initialization sets parameter values before training; Xavier/Glorot and He schemes scale initial weights by layer fan-in and fan-out. Documented effects are on gradient flow at the start of training, convergence speed and final performance.

explainer.example: A deep network with ReLU activations uses He initialization so that early-layer gradients stay in a workable range during the first epochs.
